correctness.rationale: For u=x²+y², the original rotation cancels exactly: (u,z)dot=2εy²(P,Q). On compact u>=c>0, no full unit-time orbit segment has y identically zero (it would force x=0), so compactness gives a positive lower bound on the integral of y² and the signed planar clock diverges along complete confined orbits. Pull back a planar hyperbolic-cycle isolating annulus to obtain exact invariant torus and isolation. Floquet transverse decay transfers through the positive-time clock for ε>0 (reverses for ε<0). In the polynomial example w=u-2,R=w²+z² and wP+zQ=R(1-R), so Rdot=4εy²R(1-R); the set 0<R<4 keeps u>=2-sqrt(max(R(0),1))>0 and converges to R=1 for ε>0. This is not normal-hyperbolicity or a maximum basin assertion.

A positive-radius uniform-clock lemma proves a true nonperturbative parameter boundary and the explicit nonmaximal basin is a motivated global dynamical fact; it is not a mere finite parameter test.

limitations: All nonzero ε but per-ε, not uniform rates; no arbitrary perturbation persistence or all-coupling normal hyperbolicity.
